modules.title: 4-bit Mini ALU
modules.summary: Additional exercise: a 4-bit ALU selecting add/sub/AND/XOR via a 2-bit OP code, with carry, overflow, zero, and negative flags. Your task — no reference code shown; test your own against a real simulator below.
modules.statement:
Design and implement a 4-bit Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) using Verilog HDL. The ALU takes two 4-bit inputs A and B and a 2-bit control input OP. Based on the value of OP, the ALU should perform one of the following operations:

OPOperation
00A + B
01A − B
10A AND B
11A XOR B

The ALU should generate a 4-bit output Result along with the following status flags:

  • C — carry-out flag for arithmetic operations
  • V — signed overflow flag
  • Z — zero flag, set to 1 when Result = 0000
  • N — negative flag, equal to the most significant bit of Result

Use the modules developed in today's lab wherever possible. In particular, reuse your 4-bit adder/subtractor module for arithmetic operations and use multiplexing logic to select the required result.

module ALU4(Result, C, V, Z, N, A, B, OP);

input [3:0] A, B;
input [1:0] OP;

output [3:0] Result;
output C, V, Z, N;

Write an appropriate testbench to verify all four ALU operations. Your test cases should also include at least one example each for: carry generation, signed overflow, zero result, and negative result.

Bonus: extend the ALU by adding OR, left-shift, right-shift, and signed comparison operations using a 3-bit control input.
modules.signature: module ALU4(Result, C, V, Z, N, A, B, OP);
